# Synthetic initial conditions for KITE.
#
# Adapted from `run_kite_example()` in KITE's inst/examples/example.R
# (KITE 26.10, commit 5995dd1, https://github.com/julianhinz/KITE),
# Copyright the KITE authors, GPL-3. This file is part of kite-mcp, also GPL-3.
#
# With n_countries = 3, n_sectors = 2 and seed = 1 the random draws, their
# order and the resulting tables are those of the example. For other sizes
# three choices are kite-mcp's own, since the example fixes them for 3
# countries and 2 sectors only:
#   * country codes are "c1", "c2", ... padded with zeros to equal width when
#     there are 10 or more countries ("c01" ... "c12");
#   * coalition_member is 1 for odd-numbered countries and 0 otherwise
#     (the example's c(1, 0, 1));
#   * carbon_intensity is 0.4 for the first sector, 0.1 for the second and 0
#     for any further sector (the example's c(0.4, 0.1)).
#
# The function returns the initial conditions in the order the example builds
# them, plus `price` and `carbon_intensity`, which the example adds only for
# mahlkow_wanner_2021.

kite_mcp_synthetic_baseline <- function(n_countries = 3L, n_sectors = 2L, seed = 1L) {
  set.seed(seed)
  width <- if (n_countries >= 10) nchar(as.character(n_countries)) else 1L
  countries <- sprintf(paste0("c%0", width, "d"), seq_len(n_countries))
  sectors <- paste0("s", seq_len(n_sectors))
  n_c <- length(countries); n_s <- length(sectors)

  dt_3d <- function(values, names_list) {
    grid <- data.table::CJ(d1 = names_list[[1]],
                           d2 = names_list[[2]],
                           d3 = names_list[[3]],
                           sorted = FALSE)
    data.table::setnames(grid, c("d1", "d2", "d3"), names(names_list))
    grid[, value := values][]
  }
  dt_2d <- function(values, names_list) {
    grid <- data.table::CJ(d1 = names_list[[1]], d2 = names_list[[2]], sorted = FALSE)
    data.table::setnames(grid, c("d1", "d2"), names(names_list))
    grid[, value := values][]
  }
  dt_1d <- function(values, name, levels) {
    dt <- data.table::data.table(d1 = levels, value = values)
    data.table::setnames(dt, "d1", name); dt[]
  }

  ts_arr <- array(runif(n_c * n_c * n_s, 0.3, 1), c(n_c, n_c, n_s),
                  dimnames = list(origin = countries,
                                  destination = countries,
                                  sector = sectors))
  ts_norm <- sweep(ts_arr, 2:3, apply(ts_arr, 2:3, sum), "/")
  trade_share <- dt_3d(as.numeric(aperm(ts_norm, c(3, 2, 1))),
                       list(origin = countries,
                            destination = countries,
                            sector = sectors))

  is_arr <- array(runif(n_c * n_s * n_s, 0.3, 1), c(n_c, n_s, n_s),
                  dimnames = list(country = countries,
                                  input = sectors, output = sectors))
  is_norm <- sweep(is_arr, c(1, 3), apply(is_arr, c(1, 3), sum), "/")
  intermediate_share <- dt_3d(as.numeric(aperm(is_norm, c(3, 2, 1))),
                              list(country = countries,
                                   input = sectors, output = sectors))

  factor_share <- dt_2d(
    as.numeric(t(matrix(runif(n_c * n_s, 0.25, 0.55), n_c, n_s))),
    list(country = countries, sector = sectors))

  cs_raw <- matrix(runif(n_c * n_s, 0.3, 1), n_c, n_s)
  consumption_share <- dt_2d(as.numeric(t(cs_raw / rowSums(cs_raw))),
                             list(country = countries, sector = sectors))

  expenditure <- dt_2d(
    as.numeric(t(matrix(runif(n_c * n_s, 100, 200), n_c, n_s))),
    list(destination = countries, sector = sectors))

  value_added <- dt_1d(runif(n_c, 100, 200), "country", countries)

  tb_raw <- runif(n_c, -5, 5)
  trade_balance <- dt_1d(tb_raw - mean(tb_raw), "country", countries)

  trade_elasticity <- dt_1d(runif(n_s, 4, 6), "sector", sectors)

  identity_tariff <- dt_3d(rep(1, n_c * n_c * n_s),
                           list(origin = countries,
                                destination = countries,
                                sector = sectors))

  coalition <- as.integer(seq_len(n_c) %% 2L == 1L)

  ic <- list(
    trade_share = trade_share,
    intermediate_share = intermediate_share,

       carbon_intensity = carbon_intensity)

# Synthetic initial conditions for KITE.
#
# Adapted from `run_kite_example()` in KITE's inst/examples/example.R
# (KITE 26.10, commit 5995dd1, https://github.com/julianhinz/KITE),
# Copyright the KITE authors, GPL-3. This file is part of kite-mcp, also GPL-3.
#
# With n_countries = 3, n_sectors = 2 and seed = 1 the random draws, their
# order and the resulting tables are those of the example. For other sizes
# three choices are kite-mcp's own, since the example fixes them for 3
# countries and 2 sectors only:
#   * country codes are "c1", "c2", ... padded with zeros to equal width when
#     there are 10 or more countries ("c01" ... "c12");
#   * coalition_member is 1 for odd-numbered countries and 0 otherwise
#     (the example's c(1, 0, 1));
#   * carbon_intensity is 0.4 for the first sector, 0.1 for the second and 0
#     for any further sector (the example's c(0.4, 0.1)).
#
# The function returns the initial conditions in the order the example builds
# them, plus `price` and `carbon_intensity`, which the example adds only for
# mahlkow_wanner_2021.

kite_mcp_synthetic_baseline <- function(n_countries = 3L, n_sectors = 2L, seed = 1L) {
  set.seed(seed)
  width <- if (n_countries >= 10) nchar(as.character(n_countries)) else 1L
  countries <- sprintf(paste0("c%0", width, "d"), seq_len(n_countries))
  sectors <- paste0("s", seq_len(n_sectors))
  n_c <- length(countries); n_s <- length(sectors)

  dt_3d <- function(values, names_list) {
    grid <- data.table::CJ(d1 = names_list[[1]],
                           d2 = names_list[[2]],
                           d3 = names_list[[3]],
                           sorted = FALSE)
    data.table::setnames(grid, c("d1", "d2", "d3"), names(names_list))
    grid[, value := values][]
  }
  dt_2d <- function(values, names_list) {
    grid <- data.table::CJ(d1 = names_list[[1]], d2 = names_list[[2]], sorted = FALSE)
    data.table::setnames(grid, c("d1", "d2"), names(names_list))
    grid[, value := values][]
  }
  dt_1d <- function(values, name, levels) {
    dt <- data.table::data.table(d1 = levels, value = values)
    data.table::setnames(dt, "d1", name); dt[]
  }

  ts_arr <- array(runif(n_c * n_c * n_s, 0.3, 1), c(n_c, n_c, n_s),
                  dimnames = list(origin = countries,
                                  destination = countries,
                                  sector = sectors))
  ts_norm <- sweep(ts_arr, 2:3, apply(ts_arr, 2:3, sum), "/")
  trade_share <- dt_3d(as.numeric(aperm(ts_norm, c(3, 2, 1))),
                       list(origin = countries,
                            destination = countries,
                            sector = sectors))

  is_arr <- array(runif(n_c * n_s * n_s, 0.3, 1), c(n_c, n_s, n_s),
                  dimnames = list(country = countries,
                                  input = sectors, output = sectors))
  is_norm <- sweep(is_arr, c(1, 3), apply(is_arr, c(1, 3), sum), "/")
  intermediate_share <- dt_3d(as.numeric(aperm(is_norm, c(3, 2, 1))),
                              list(country = countries,
                                   input = sectors, output = sectors))

  factor_share <- dt_2d(
    as.numeric(t(matrix(runif(n_c * n_s, 0.25, 0.55), n_c, n_s))),
    list(country = countries, sector = sectors))

  cs_raw <- matrix(runif(n_c * n_s, 0.3, 1), n_c, n_s)
  consumption_share <- dt_2d(as.numeric(t(cs_raw / rowSums(cs_raw))),
                             list(country = countries, sector = sectors))

  expenditure <- dt_2d(
    as.numeric(t(matrix(runif(n_c * n_s, 100, 200), n_c, n_s))),
    list(destination = countries, sector = sectors))

  value_added <- dt_1d(runif(n_c, 100, 200), "country", countries)

  tb_raw <- runif(n_c, -5, 5)
  trade_balance <- dt_1d(tb_raw - mean(tb_raw), "country", countries)

  trade_elasticity <- dt_1d(runif(n_s, 4, 6), "sector", sectors)

  identity_tariff <- dt_3d(rep(1, n_c * n_c * n_s),
                           list(origin = countries,
                                destination = countries,
                                sector = sectors))

  coalition <- as.integer(seq_len(n_c) %% 2L == 1L)

  ic <- list(
    trade_share = trade_share,
    intermediate_share = intermediate_share,
    factor_share = factor_share,
    consumption_share = consumption_share,
    expenditure = expenditure,
    value_added = value_added,
    trade_balance = trade_balance,
    elasticities = list(trade_elasticity = trade_elasticity),
    tariff = identity_tariff,
    ntb = data.table::copy(identity_tariff),
    export_subsidy = data.table::copy(identity_tariff),
    coalition_member = dt_1d(coalition, "country", countries)
  )

  # drawn after the scenario-independent tables, as in the example
  price <- dt_2d(runif(n_c * n_s, 0.8, 1.2),
                 list(country = countries, sector = sectors))
  intensity <- c(0.4, 0.1, rep(0, max(0L, n_s - 2L)))[seq_len(n_s)]
  carbon_intensity <- dt_1d(intensity, "sector", sectors)

  list(initial_conditions = ic,
       price = price,
       carbon_intensity = carbon_intensity)
}

baseline <- kite_mcp_synthetic_baseline(n_countries = 3L, n_sectors = 2L, seed = 1L)
ic <- baseline$initial_conditions
countries <- c("c1", "c2", "c3")
sectors <- c("s1", "s2")

# ---- scenario ----------------------------------------------------------------

model_scenario <- list()
settings <- list(verbose = 0L, tolerance = 0.0001, vfactor = 0.1, max_iterations = 200.0)

# ---- run -----------------------------------------------------------------------

result <- update_equilibrium(model = caliendo_parro_2015, initial_conditions = ic,
                             model_scenario = model_scenario, settings = settings)
processed <- process_results(result)

info <- result$info
cat("convergence:", format(info$convergence), "| iterations:", info$iterations,
    "| criterion:", format(info$criterion, digits = 17), "\n")
cat("accounting:", format(info$accounting$ok), "-", info$accounting$reason, "\n")
for (name in names(processed$output)) {
  cat("\n==", name, "==\n")
  print(processed$output[[name]], digits = 17, nrows = Inf)
}

out <- Sys.getenv("KITE_MCP_REPRODUCE_OUT")
if (nzchar(out)) saveRDS(list(info = info, output = processed$output), out)

# Welfare effects of 20 % reciprocal tariffs between c1 and c2 (caliendo_parro_2015, synthetic_example)

c1 and c2 both lose welfare from the tariffs, and c3, the outside country, gains. c2 loses more than c1 once the baseline's own adjustment is removed.

**Setup.** `tariff_new` = 1.2 on every sector in both directions: c2 on imports from c1, and c1 on imports from c2. All other tariffs stay at their baseline level of 1. The synthetic baseline isn't an equilibrium of the model, so even an empty scenario moves welfare. I ran an empty-scenario reference and compared the two runs to separate the tariff effect from that adjustment.

## Convergence
Both runs converged, with no warnings and the accounting check passing.

| Run | run_id | status | iterations | criterion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tariff scenario | r2f481dc1e52a | converged | 22 | 9.757e-05 |
| Reference (empty scenario) | r6950dfd96970 | converged | 20 | 8.760e-05 |

The tolerance was 1e-4 in both runs. In both info blocks the accounting rule is `fixed` and `ok` is true, with the reason "the solved trade balances sum to zero for the world". `baseline_world_trade_balance` is 0, `world_trade_balance` is 0 and the accounting tolerance is 1e-06. `world_value_added` is 490.26744994553644 in the tariff run and 490.26536844670864 in the reference run.

**Warnings:** KITE raised none in either run.

## Welfare by country
The values come from the `welfare_change` table, read with `compare_runs` (run_a = reference, run_b = tariff scenario). Each value is a ratio of counterfactual to the original baseline, so 1 means no change.

| Country | Reference run (value_a) | Tariff run (value_b) | difference_derived |
|---|---|---|---|
| c1 | 0.9016684493436061 | 0.8516332754471132 | -0.050035173896492924 |
| c2 | 0.9960473177440451 | 0.9208435240405587 | -0.0752037937034864 |
| c3 | 1.0915254666205483 | 1.1449932563292378 | 0.053467789708689484 |

- **Tariff effect (`difference_derived`):** kite-mcp computed this column, not KITE, as value_b − value_a. It is a difference of two ratios, both measured against the original baseline, so it is not itself a ratio.
- **Who wins and loses:** both tariff-setting countries come out below the reference run, with c2 losing more than c1. c3 gains, which fits trade being diverted to it.
- **Tariff run on its own:** `run_scenario` reports `percent_change_derived` (also computed by kite-mcp) for the `welfare_change` values above: c1 −14.84 %, c2 −7.92 %, c3 +14.50 %. These figures mix the tariff effect with the baseline's own adjustment, so read them alongside the reference column.

## Baseline note
The `synthetic_example` baseline is made-up data and describes no real economy. `run_scenario` returned this note: *"Synthetic data generated from random draws, as in KITE's inst/examples/example.R. It describes no real economy, and its numbers have no real-world units. The construction draws value added independently of the trade and production shares, so the baseline is not an equilibrium of the models: a run with an empty scenario does not give welfare_change = 1, and every run's results include this adjustment of the baseline as well as the policy."*

## Reproduce
These R scripts rerun each scenario with KITE 26.10 (commit 5995dd1) without this server:
- Tariff scenario: `kite://runs/r2f481dc1e52a/reproduce.R`
- Reference run: `kite://runs/r6950dfd96970/reproduce.R`
